title: Symmetry Reveals the In-Context Classifier: Transformers Implement Mean-Shift Dynamics
claim: Imposing symmetry makes a model's learned computation identifiable, exposing structured weights that read as an explicit iterative algorithm.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, colored title boxes, equations and heatmaps
description: Three bordered panels read left to right, each with a colored title box: purple 'Symmetry constraint', orange 'Interpretable weights', green 'Emergent algorithm'. The left panel shows a 'permutation sandwich': Z_l flows through P, Attention, then P-transpose to Z_{l+1}, with a dashed skip arrow over the top. Below are three small icons labeled same predictions (scatter along a diagonal), same response to query perturbations, and same influential examples (bar charts). The middle panel shows a noisy red/blue weight heatmap without permutations, an arrow, and a clean block-diagonal heatmap with permutations. Beneath it is the canonical block matrix W ≈ [αI, 0; 0, γ(I − 11ᵀ/K)]. The right panel shows the update equations for A_l, X_{l+1} and Y_{l+1} in a green box, 'depth ↔ iterations', and a small cartoon of blue and red points moving apart.
caption: Symmetry reveals coupled mean-shift inference in transformers. Left: Enforcing feature/label permutation symmetry layer by layer preserves the inference rule: we match predictions, response to query perturbations (local decision rule), and influential examples (context sensitivity). Middle: The symmetry constraint denoises weights into a canonical low-dimensional structure. Right: The resulting structure makes the forward pass readable as a closed-form iterative classifier (depth ↔iterations), yielding a geometry-driven algorithmic motif in which features and labels co-evolve.
abstract: Transformers can perform in-context classification from a few labeled examples, yet the inference-time algorithm remains opaque. We study multi-class linear classification in the hard no-margin regime and make the computation identifiable by enforcing feature- and label-permutation equivariance at every layer. This enables interpretability while maintaining functional equivalence and yields highly structured weights. From these models we extract an explicit depth-indexed recursion---an end-to-end identified, emergent update rule inside a standard softmax transformer, to our knowledge the first of its kind. Attention matrices formed from mixed feature--label Gram structure drive coupled updates of training points, labels, and the test probe. The resulting dynamics implement label-aware mean-shift, which provably amplifies class separation and yields robust expected class alignment.
